case.pattern_description: Coordinated shared-device ring: a single mobile device fingerprint, always reached through an anonymising proxy, appears on many unrelated cardholders' accounts within a few weeks and is marked New for every one of them. case.summary: Analyst request on card C13487-K1: $74.96 online on 2016-11-22, scored 0.05 by the bank's model. The device profile is shared by 28 unrelated cards within 30 days, marked new for 100% of transactions, and consistently behind IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS, while online accounts for 2.8% of this card's history. Activity occurred on both channels within 48 hours with 2 identity anomalies (new device=False, device marked New=True, match flag=match_status:2, proxy=IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS, new email domain=False), alongside matching closed cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035. Assessed as fraud at probability 0.98 with an exposure of $439.61. Recommended actions: BLOCK_CARD (L1), MONITOR_CARD (auto), MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS (auto), CREATE_CASE (auto), FILE_REPORT (L2), ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST (auto).

sar.narrative: Customer C13487, holder of card C13487-K1, was subject to a flagged online transaction on 2016-11-22 16:11:00 for the amount of $74.96 under product code C. This activity was determined to be fraud with a probability of 0.98, an undocumented pattern, and a total exposure of $439.61. The suspicion arises because the transaction originated from a device profile shared by 28 unrelated cards within 30 days, marked new for 100% of the transactions it ever appears on, and consistently behind IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS. This contrasts with the card's established behavior of 71 prior transactions where online accounts for only 3% of activity, despite the bank's model scoring the transaction at 0.05. Further evidence of coordination is established through matching closed cases CC-2649, CC-2971, CC-2985, and CC-3035 which share the same device profile and undocumented typology. Recommended actions for this incident include BLOCK_CARD, MONITOR_CARD, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT, and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST. Any customer response was simulated.

risk.calibration_note: trigger prior for analyst_request (+0.00 log-odds) plus a logistic combination of detector strengths; coefficients fitted on 8065 closed cases. The intercept is a per-trigger prior rather than one global constant. Measured on the shipped history, all 900 cleared investigations began as a model score and every investigated customer dispute was confirmed fraud; the README states that most high scores are legitimate and that half the exam pack is. A model-score alert therefore starts at p=0.17, a customer dispute at p=0.73 and an analyst request at p=0.50, and graph evidence moves it from there.

findings.name: card_testing
findings.limitations: Probes of $2-$5 are not separable from ordinary small online purchases, so card testing done with them is missed by design; catching it would flag 2.4% of legitimate high-score alerts.

findings.name: sub_threshold_structuring
findings.why: no run of 3+ online purchases clustered just under a round authorisation threshold
findings.limitations: A single merchant with fixed high-value pricing could produce similar amounts; the sub-threshold clustering plus the short span is what distinguishes it.

findings.name: shared_device_ring
findings.why: device profile shared by 28 unrelated cards within 30 days, marked New for 100% of the transactions it ever appears on, and consistently behind IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS
findings.limitations: Device profiles are coarse fingerprints (model + OS + browser + screen) and common desktop fingerprints are shared by many unrelated customers. What isolates this one is that it is New for every account it touches and always proxied.

findings.name: account_takeover
findings.why: activity on both channels within 48 hours with 2 identity anomalies (new device=False, device marked New=True, match flag=match_status:2, proxy=IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS, new email domain=False)
findings.limitations: Mixed-channel use is normal for many cardholders; this detector requires identity anomalies on top of the channel mix.

findings.name: recurring_charge
findings.limitations: A fraudster repeating an identical amount monthly would look the same; the cardholder should still be asked to confirm (policy R7 says verify, not block).

findings.name: consistent_with_history
findings.why: $74.96 is at or below the card's 95th-percentile amount ($107.99); 36 prior transactions in billing region 191; device profile already seen 1 times on this card
findings.limitations: A compromised card used carefully within the cardholder's normal envelope would also look like this.

policy_rules.R1: Verify before blocking on a weak signal: a single signal with assessed probability below 0.70 gets VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER or STEP_UP_AUTH first.
policy_rules.R2: Customer denies: BLOCK_CARD and CREATE_CASE; add FILE_REPORT if exposure exceeds $1,000 or the case connects to a shared device profile or another card's fraud.
policy_rules.R3: Customer confirms: CLOSE_NO_FRAUD, noting the confirmation.
policy_rules.R4: No reply within 24 hours: MONITOR_CARD and DECLINE_TRANSACTION for pending authorisations; escalate if exposure exceeds $500.
policy_rules.R5: Card testing: DECLINE_TRANSACTION and STEP_UP_AUTH; BLOCK_CARD if a purchase over $100 has already cleared.
policy_rules.R6: Shared origin: name the shared element, CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT and MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS for every card that shares it.
policy_rules.R7: Disputed but legitimate: CREATE_CASE, VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER and WARN_CUSTOMER. Do not block.
policy_rules.R8: Escalate when uncertain and exposed: verdict uncertain with exposure over $500, or conflicting evidence, gets ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST.
policy_rules.R9: Undocumented patterns: CREATE_CASE, FILE_REPORT and ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST, described in the agent's own words.
policy_rules.R10: Never BLOCK_ALL_CARDS unless at least two of the customer's cards show confirmed fraud or credentials are confirmed compromised.
policy_rules.3a: Open a case whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever evidence is requested, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A report is a separate, external filing.
policy_rules.6: Stop when probability is at or above 0.85 or at or below 0.15 with at least two independent pieces of evidence, when a verification response settles the question, or when further steps would not change the decision.

action_effects.DECLINE_TRANSACTION: decline the pending authorisation at the switch
action_effects.MONITOR_CARD: raise the card's monitoring sensitivity for 72 hours
action_effects.MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS: raise monitoring on every linked card
action_effects.WARN_CUSTOMER: send an informational message to the cardholder
action_effects.VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER: ask the cardholder to confirm the transaction
action_effects.STEP_UP_AUTH: require a one-time passcode before further activity
action_effects.BLOCK_CARD: block the card and queue a reissue
action_effects.BLOCK_ALL_CARDS: block every card the customer holds
action_effects.GENERATE_REPORT: write the investigation to the internal record
action_effects.FILE_REPORT: submit a suspicious activity report to the regulator
action_effects.ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST: hand the case to a human analyst queue
